```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(AKCatchments)
options(AKCatchments.cache = file.path(tempdir(), "ak_vignette_cache"))
```

Shares of permafrost extent classes (continuous, discontinuous, sporadic,
isolated) and ground-ice classes, and a total permafrost estimate with
uncertainty, from the Permafrost Characteristics of Alaska map (Jorgenson
et al. 2008), the source of the NPS catchment descriptors' permafrost
columns.

Input, as for every layer: catchments (sf polygons with `site_code`, one
row per catchment, any CRS; a single `ak_delineate()` result, a list of
them, `ak_catchments()` output or your own polygons). Chunks that download
data are not run when this vignette is built; chunks that only compute
are. The other layers are listed in `vignette("delineation")`, section 7.

## 1. Getting the data

**Downloaded once.** The shapefile (13 MB, North Slope Science Catalog
dataset 1725) is downloaded into the cache's `jorgenson_2008/` folder the
first time it is needed; or pass `path` to a copy of your own. Citation and
terms: `ak_citations(layers = "permafrost")` and `vignette("data-sources")`.

```{r download, eval = FALSE}
ak_prefetch(x, layers = "permafrost/jorgenson2008")   # downloads it now
```

The 2008 shapefile codes extent as letters in `PF_EXTENT` (C, D, S, I,
plus G glacier, U unfrozen, W water); other versions with class names work
too (`ext_field`, `ice_field` override the detection).

## 2. Using it

```{r use, eval = FALSE}
d <- ak_delineate(lat = 63.7255, lon = -148.9670, site_code = "SITE-001")   # one catchment
ak_permafrost(d)                                     # one catchment: its row with the columns added

x <- ak_catchments(pts)                                  # many: data frame of site_code, lat, lon
x <- ak_permafrost(x)                            # columns appended to x, provenance recorded
ak_provenance(x)

ak_permafrost(sf::read_sf("hand_catchments.gpkg"))            # your own polygons with site_code (or import_catchments())
```

The ground-ice shares (`groundice_pct_*`) come with them. `sigma_m`
(positional SD, default 1000 m) and `n` (draws, 500) set the simulation;
`sigma_m = 0` keeps only the class ranges.

## 3. What you get

`jorg_pct_<class>` (percent of the whole catchment), `jorg_pct_coverage_pct`,
`groundice_pct_<class>`, `totperm_pct` (class-midpoint estimate),
`totperm_pct_se`, `totperm_pct_lo95`, `totperm_pct_hi95`,
`totperm_pct_flag` (`jitter_dominates`).

## 4. Uncertainty: how it is computed

**Product error (P).** The map gives extent classes, each a range of
permafrost fraction: continuous 90-100%, discontinuous 50-90%, sporadic
10-50%, isolated 1-10% (the package's lower bound for isolated is 1%; the
class definition is under 10%, so 0-10% is the alternative). Its
catalogue entry warns of 1-3 km horizontal error.

**Calculation.** 500 draws, each combining:

- a random shift of the catchment against the map, N(0, `sigma_m`) in x
  and y (`sigma_m = 1000` by default: median shift 1.2 km, 90th
  percentile 2.1 km);
- a permafrost fraction for each class drawn uniformly within its range.

`totperm_pct` is the class-midpoint estimate on the mapped shares;
`_se`, `_lo95`, `_hi95` summarise the draws. `totperm_pct_flag` says
`jitter_dominates` where the shift part of the spread is larger than the
class-range part: the map's placement, not its class definitions, sets
the uncertainty there (usually small catchments near class boundaries).

```{r rayleigh}
sigma <- 1000
c(median_shift_m = sigma * sqrt(2 * log(2)), p90_shift_m = sigma * sqrt(-2 * log(0.1)))
```

**Assumptions and alternatives.**

- Uniform within class. A distribution concentrated near the class centre
  (triangular, beta) gives smaller SEs; uniform is the cautious choice.
- The class fractions are drawn once per draw for all sites, so the
  class-range part is shared between sites (a systematic error: if
  "discontinuous" really means 60%, it means it everywhere). Per-site
  marginal SEs don't depend on this, but between-site differences are
  more certain than the per-site SEs suggest.
- A rigid shift of the whole catchment treats the map's error as uniform
  across the catchment. Independent errors on each boundary would give
  less spread in large catchments.
- `sigma_m` is the dominant choice for small catchments; rerun with 500
  and 2000 m to see how much it matters.
- Pastick et al. (2015) is an independent estimate of the same thing; the
  difference between the two products is a third view of the uncertainty.

### Ground ice

`groundice_pct_*` are class shares from the same map, with the same
positional error. No SE is computed by default; run
`positional_uncertainty()` on the map with the ground-ice field to get
one.

## 5. Checking and validating it

- **Against the NPS descriptors.** For CAKN sites, `totperm_pct` should
  match the NPS per*perm columns where the polygons are the same.
- **Against Pastick.** An independent model of a related quantity
  (near-surface permafrost probability):

```{r compare, eval = FALSE}
ak_permafrost(x) |> ak_permafrost(source = "pastick2015") |>   # both maps on the same catchments
  dplyr::select(site_code, totperm_pct, totperm_pct_lo95, totperm_pct_hi95, pf_prob_mean, pf_land_lo, pf_land_hi)
```

  Disagreement beyond both products' ranges points at sites where neither
  should be trusted.
- **Sensitivity to `sigma_m`.** Rerun with 500 and 2000 m.

## 6. Pitfalls

- 1-3 km positional error against catchments of a few km²: small
  catchments near class boundaries can be wholly misassigned.
- Extent classes are ranges, not measurements; the midpoint is a choice.
- The class-range part of the error is shared between sites (section 4 above).

## References

- Jorgenson, T. et al. (2008). Permafrost characteristics of Alaska. Proceedings of the Ninth International Conference on Permafrost, extended abstracts. Data: North Slope Science Catalog, dataset 1725.
